findings.title: Failure-pattern harvest misses valid fix tasks
findings.desc: Harvest eligibility is inferred solely from the branch tip subject matching `fix:`/`fix(...)`, although conventional prefixes are only preferred and a final retro/docs commit may follow an earlier fix commit. Such tasks can contain the required `Failure pattern:` note yet be silently excluded.

findings.title: Harvest commit failures are silently ignored
findings.desc: The generated commit omits the required autonomous `Confidence:`/`Notes:` body, and `git commit ... || true` suppresses hook or other failures. A failure leaves `failure-patterns.md` staged and the repository dirty, potentially contaminating later loop operations.

findings.title: Unvalidated post-gate LLM write
findings.desc: The script asks a tool-capable Claude invocation to consume task-authored retros and then commits its output after all validation gates, without verifying that the change is append-only or schema-conformant. Prompt injection or model error can therefore modify the failure-pattern library—and potentially leave other repository changes—without review.

findings.title: Harvest commit violates autonomous commit format
findings.desc: The scripted `/away` commit has only a subject and omits the newly required `Confidence:` and `Notes:` body fields, so the loop's own generated commit does not follow the process this change documents.

findings.title: Valid breaking fix commits are not harvested
findings.desc: The subject filter recognizes only `fix:` and `fix(scope)` forms, excluding valid Conventional Commit forms such as `fix!:` and `fix(scope)!:`; retros from those approved fix tasks will never contribute failure patterns.

findings.title: Unvalidated LLM output bypasses merge gates
findings.desc: The post-merge Claude invocation reads agent-authored retros and has unrestricted repository tooling on main, with no mechanical append-only or path validation. Its failure is ignored, and any resulting change to the failure-pattern library is committed even after a partial/erroring run, allowing prompt injection or malformed output to bypass all prior validation.

findings.title: Harvest commit violates autonomous commit format
findings.desc: The generated commit has only a subject despite the newly documented requirement that autonomous commits include `Confidence:` and `Notes:`. Suppressing commit errors can also leave the failure-pattern file staged and silently contaminate later operations.

findings.title: Optional commit naming controls pattern harvesting
findings.desc: Retros are harvested only when the final subject matches `fix:` or `fix(...)`, although the task prompt merely prefers conventional prefixes and valid forms such as `fix!:` or `fix(scope)!:` are also excluded. Root-caused fixes with other descriptive subjects will therefore never reach the failure-pattern library.

findings.title: Decision record documents unshipped code
findings.desc: The record (and log.md entry 20) describes Tier B/A changes — a new gate 1h running `skills/code-review` on task branches, `parse_code_review_red`/`code_review_gate_verdict` extracted to `si-functions.sh` with unit tests, and `file_scope` (gate 1c) widened to allow `docs/decisions/`, `docs/reviews/`, `docs/thoughts/` — none of which appear in this diff. Only the implement-prompt text and the post-merge harvest step were actually added to `scripts/self-improvement.sh`; `si-functions.sh` is untouched, so the decision doc materially overclaims what shipped in this commit.

findings.title: Harvest step's git commands not scoped to repo dir
findings.desc: `git log -1 --format=%s "$TIP_SHA"`, `git diff --quiet -- "$FP_LIB"`, `git add`, and `git commit` are invoked without `-C "$REPO_DIR"` or a preceding `cd`, while `FP_LIB`/`RETRO` paths are explicitly qualified with `$REPO_DIR`. If the script's CWD at this point isn't `$REPO_DIR` (plausible given other steps reference `$WORKING_DIR`), these git calls will silently fail or target the wrong working tree/branch.

findings.title: Harvest failures are silently swallowed
findings.desc: The `claude -p ... 2>/dev/null || true` and `git commit ... 2>/dev/null || true` suppress all output and error status, so a failed harvest (bad claude invocation, commit failure, etc.) produces no diagnostic and the round proceeds as if harvesting succeeded, undermining the "cross-round learning" goal described in the decision doc.

findings.title: Fix-commit detection is a brittle prefix heuristic
findings.desc: Only commit subjects starting with `fix:` or `fix(` are treated as bug-fix tasks eligible for failure-pattern harvesting; any approved fix whose final commit subject doesn't follow the conventional-commit prefix (despite the prompt only "preferring" it, not requiring it) is silently excluded from the failure-pattern library.

findings.title: git log run without explicit repo path
findings.desc: `git log -1 --format=%s "$TIP_SHA"` is invoked without `-C "$REPO_DIR"` or a `cd`, unlike other operations in this block that explicitly qualify paths with `$REPO_DIR`; if the script's cwd differs from `$REPO_DIR` (e.g. when called from a worktree or a different working directory), this silently returns an empty subject via the `|| echo ""` fallback, causing fix-commit detection to fail and failure patterns to be silently dropped without any error.

findings.title: Harvest failures are fully swallowed
findings.desc: The `claude -p ...` call redirects stderr to `/dev/null` and appends `|| true`, and the subsequent commit also uses `|| true`; any failure in the harvest step (bad prompt, claude CLI error, git failure) is invisible to the operator, so failure-pattern harvesting can silently stop working across rounds with no diagnostic trail.

findings.title: Harvest step trusts LLM output without verifying "do not modify existing entries" constraint
findings.desc: The harvest prompt instructs claude not to modify existing failure-pattern entries, but the script only checks `git diff --quiet` to decide whether to commit — it never verifies that only new FP-NNN entries were appended versus existing text being altered, so a hallucinated edit to prior entries would be committed to main automatically.

findings.title: Silent failure swallowing on harvest call
findings.desc: `claude -p ... 2>/dev/null || true` discards all error output and return status, so a persistently failing/misconfigured harvest step (e.g., auth failure, bad prompt) will fail silently every round with no diagnostic trail.

findings.title: Passing file paths to LLM instead of contents
findings.desc: The script interpolates a list of file paths (`$FIX_RETROS`) into the CLI prompt string. Unless the `claude` CLI behaves as an autonomous agent that automatically reads system paths mentioned in text, the LLM will only see the paths themselves and won't have the retro content needed to extract failure patterns.
